Thought: We need to balance the chemical equation to determine the value of \( x \) in the reaction of CaSiO3 with dilute hydrochloric acid. The initial unbalanced equation is:

\[ \text{CaSiO}_3 + 2\text{HCl} + x\text{H}_2\text{O} \rightarrow \text{SiO}_2 \cdot 11\text{H}_2\text{O} + \text{CaCl}_2 \]

To balance the equation, we will match the number of atoms of each element on the reactant side with the product side. We are particularly interested in the water molecules, which will give us the value of \( x \).

1. On the product side, the compound \(\text{SiO}_2 \cdot 11\text{H}_2\text{O}\) indicates there are already 11 water molecules.
2. Therefore, to balance the equation, \( x \) must be equivalent to the number of water molecules needed to supply the 11 waters in the product.
Final Answer: [ANSWER]11[/ANSWER]
